corrections.new:
For the serving assembly — `handle` and its region functions — and the exchange machine it
drives:

Every `ExchangeEvent` the machine learns of reaches it in one of exactly two ways. A
STAGE-OWNED event travels inside an `Established<T>`: the carrier is constructed at the site
the stage's work returned its product, has no public field and no reader other than
`ExchangeProgress::establish` and, for the notification terminal's carrier,
`ServedSuccess::tail`, which reads its event alone — for `may_publish` to check before the 202
is signed and for `publish` to advance after the outcome commitment and retention, the product
never yielded — and is `#[must_use]`, so the assembly cannot obtain the product without the
machine advancing the event in the same step and cannot discard the product without a warning
the build refuses. An
ASSEMBLY-OWNED event is stated by a direct `advance` in the serving path, and the set of events
stated that way is exactly the three inventoried with the reason no stage's success could carry
each: `BackendDispatched`, `ContinuationRetired`, `ContinuationNotRequired`. The success tail —
`EvidenceRetained`, then `TerminalResponseServed` or `OpenLegResponseServed` — is advanced only
by `PublishPermit::publish`, after `may_publish` has checked the same tail, and the serving
path advances none of them itself.

The two sets are disjoint: no event a stage establishes is also advanced by the serving path,
so no stage's fact is stated twice or remembered beside the carrier. The assembly-owned set is
measured in both directions — an advance naming an event outside the three, and a listed event
the serving path no longer advances, are each a failing control — so a deleted assembly-owned
`advance` is detected, not merely forbidden.

Legality is THM-0043's: every advance, by either route, is checked against the relation in
every build and latches an anomaly when refused. What this theorem adds is that for the
stage-owned events the machine's state implies the stage's product was obtained, and for the
three it names, and only those, the correspondence rests on the assembly's own statement.

corrections.reason: THM-0101, in this theorem's dependency closure, field statement. One clause names `PublishPermit::publish`, the consumer of the permit `may_publish` returns, in place of `ExchangeProgress::publish`, which #1253 deleted. The tail it names, the check before it and the serving path's exclusion are unchanged, and the corrected text states nothing stronger. The owner accepted this correction in the ruling of 2026-10-27.

dependency_correction: No edge added or removed; depends_on is unchanged. The dependency digest moved solely because THM-0101's claim digest moved.
reason: DEPENDENCY PROPAGATION of the THM-0101 wording correction. THM-0136's own statement, security_consequence, scope, severity, depends_on and review requirement are byte-identical to the reviewed text; its fingerprint moved only through the claim digest of THM-0101, which the owner accepted on 2026-10-27. The owner has not individually reviewed THM-0136 at this fingerprint. The owner's ruling covers THM-0101 and THM-0074; THM-0136 was not named in the packet's inventory, and this record carries it under the Phase-1 ruling rather than asserting an owner review.
ruling: ADR-MCPRE-068 Phase-1 campaign ruling, 2026-09-18 (dependency corrections that leave the accepted promise intact are not owner escalations), applied to the dependency propagation of the THM-0101 correction the owner accepted in the ruling of 2026-10-27 on #1258 (verification/reviews/rulings/thm-0101-permit-publish-2026-10-27.md). A correction record is not an approval: it does not make the specification-review axis fresh, and release-mode establishment still asks for the owner.
subject: THM-0136
